title: The first screen a user ever sees ignores dark mode entirely
detail: useTheme is called only inside AppShell, but ProfilePicker renders outside the router and outside AppShell. Nothing sets the `dark` class on <html> on that screen, so its dark:bg-night and dark:text-* classes never activate — the 'Who's reading?' screen is always light, including for a user whose system and stored preference are both dark.

title: Dark mode is applied in an effect, so dark-mode users get a white flash on every load
detail: The `dark` class is toggled after React mounts and after the profile resolves from IndexedDB — which means a full paint of the light theme first. The stored preference lives on the profile record in IndexedDB, so it cannot be read synchronously; without an inline pre-hydration script keyed off a mirrored localStorage value, the flash is unavoidable.

title: Daily Wisdom can pick a book with no summary and show an empty quote
detail: The pool is Finished books, falling back to all books, with no filter for having a summary. For a library built from Goodreads import — where nothing is summarised by design — the modal appears once a day to announce 'This book has no summary yet.'

title: REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION — the carousel does correctly what three other surfaces get wrong
detail: It makes the card itself a <button> so it is keyboard reachable, marks the decorative hover panel aria-hidden, labels both scroll controls, adds a focus-visible ring, and gives every img an onError fallback. BookCard (S161), StatCard (S112) and the PDF drop zone (S065) each re-solve the same problem as a bare div, and BookDetail (S162) omits the cover fallback. The pattern to copy already exists in the repo.

title: Daily Wisdom's primary button is dark-on-dark, and its close button is white-on-white
detail: Line 90 is bg-gray-900 text-white with no dark variant on a dark:bg-gray-900 panel. Line 42 is the codemod casualty from S047 — bg-white with text-white — confirmed here by reading rather than by grep. Both controls on the modal are invisible in one theme or the other.

title: The book row is a div onClick duplicating the button below it
detail: Not keyboard reachable, but the 'Read Summary' button does the same thing, so it is redundant rather than blocking. It also renders an img with no onError fallback.

title: Carousel scrolls a hardcoded 340px against cards that are 280px or 320px wide
detail: The scroll step matches neither breakpoint, so paging always lands mid-card. The card widths are themselves inline literals rather than shared constants.

title: Recommendations are keyed by title
detail: key={rec.title} collides if the model returns the same title twice in one batch, which is plausible given no dedup on the response.
